minutes.headline: Select Board approved propane tank licenses for a Northfield Road farm and new building permit fees effective Jan 1, 2024.
minutes.summary: The board held a public hearing on propane storage for a family farm greenhouse operation and approved both licenses by roll call. It also approved new building, plumbing, electrical and gas permit fees, renewed annual licenses (with conditions on one establishment tied to a sewer payment plan), and discussed the MUNIS billing problems affecting sewer bills. The town manager's report and a discussion of a resident's repeated requests rounded out the night.

public_comment.topic: Asked whether there would be a presentation before questions on the propane hearing; told the hearing would come later on the agenda.
During the hearing, asked about above-ground versus underground tanks, safety, asphyxiation, and location relative to his house on Highland Street.

votes.outcome: passed (roll call, all yes as heard)
adjourned at 8:49 (roll call; count not fully audible)

budget_items.what_was_said: Plumbing, wiring and electrical inspector fees run through a revolving fund so there is no budget impact; the Building Commissioner is salaried, so the effect on revenue is positive.

budget_items.topic: Fair Share Amendment funds and Chapter 90
budget_items.what_was_said: The state announced additional Fair Share money for local infrastructure; Lunenburg's apportionment was stated alongside its Chapter 90 apportionment.
A new Treasury interim rule defines obligation as requiring contracts by the end of 2024; the town manager submitted a comment opposing it.
The establishment agreed to a weekly payment plan on back sewer charges, to be paid in full by May.
Board committed the second quarter water billing.
Payroll and accounts payable warrants and adjustments were read and signed.
Sewer billing problems after the MUNIS migration; the board wants a root cause analysis and possibly a discount at renewal.
The water district will vote on funding for a test treatment plant and voting rule changes.

decisions.decision: Reboot licenses to be conditioned on a May 21 status review before the board.
Town manager asked to give an ARPA distribution update at the second January meeting.
Board will formalize a policy asking the assessors for all tax bills and year-over-year summaries before tax classification.
A resident's request to meet will be scheduled for about 30 minutes at the next meeting.
Select Board bylaws review targeted for the third meeting in January.
Next meeting January 9; three meetings planned in January.

what_happened.line: The Select Board approved licenses for propane tank storage at two Northfield Road addresses after a long public hearing, by roll call with all yes as heard.
The board approved new building department permit fees, effective January 1, 2024, by roll call.
Annual common victualler, entertainment and alcohol license renewals passed, with one establishment, La Balina LLC (the Reboot), taken up separately.
The Reboot's licenses were tied to a sewer back-payment plan and a May 21 status review; the minutes record the vote outcome as not audible.
The board heard a Sewer Commission letter on billing problems after the MUNIS conversion and committed the second quarter water billing.

why_it_matters: Permit fees for building, plumbing, electrical and gas work change for anyone pulling a permit from January 1, 2024.
Sewer bills were affected by the MUNIS billing conversion, and the board wants a root cause analysis, so residents with sewer charges may see corrections or a renewal discount discussed later.
watch_next: Second January meeting: the town manager's ARPA distribution update, and the third January meeting: Select Board bylaws review.
May 21 at 7:10 p.m.: the Reboot's scheduled status review before the board on its sewer payment plan.
